title: The Republic of Verna
subtitle: Vernan society and visual identity
summary: Orchards and observatories, pale stone and slate, deep green and gold, spectacles and satchels, and a country that would like you to know it is not a campus.
content:
> *"No, I do not teach philosophy."*
> — a Vernan farmer, for the hundredth time

The **Republic of Verna** is more than a university with a flag. It is a prosperous, cultivated, compact country of farmers, merchants, craftspeople, printers, doctors, instrument-makers, civil servants, labourers, students and, yes, academics. Foreigners tend to remember only the last group. Vernans would like them to notice the rest.

This entry describes how [Verna](factions.html#verna) looks and how its people carry themselves. For its history and neutrality, see [[verna-and-the-university|Verna and the University]]. For the University itself, see [[university-of-verna|The University of Verna]].

> **In an orchard outside a Vernan hill town**
>
> The foreign visitor had been very polite about the view. "And which faculty do you teach in?"
>
> "No," said the farmer, "I do not teach philosophy."
>
> "Oh. What do you do?"
>
> "Grow pears."
>
> "Ah."
>
> The farmer went back to his ladder. After a moment he added, over his shoulder: "The University buys a remarkable number of pears."

## A Landscape Shaped by Generations

Verna is **temperate**, **hilly**, **cultivated** and **densely settled**: fertile valleys, rivers, vineyards and orchards, hill towns, old roads and stone bridges, with observatories, libraries and university districts set among them. Nothing in Verna feels like wilderness. It feels like land that has been lived on, farmed and studied carefully for a very long time.

![A Vernan university town above its lake](data/images/verna-homeland-45f9a531.jpg "A Vernan town in spring. Notice the restraint: pale stone and slate roofs rather than gold, an observatory dome and library towers among the trees, a glass botanical house beside a fountain garden, stone stairways and colonnades crowded with students in green, armillary spheres on the terraces, and bridges carrying the old roads across the water.")

## Stone, Slate and Gardens

Vernan architecture is **scholarly**, **civic**, **elegant** and **restrained**. Its common elements are warm **pale stone**, **slate roofs**, **courtyards**, **colonnades**, **stone stairways**, **library towers**, **observatory domes**, **botanical gardens** and **civic fountains**. Vernans have little taste for imperial monumentality. A Vernan building is meant to be lived and worked in for centuries, not to impress a visiting ambassador, although it usually manages both.

## Colours and Emblems

The Vernan palette is **deep green**, **ivory**, **gold** and **slate blue**, with **burgundy** accents. Deep green above all is the colour of Verna: on banners, robes, coats and the Republic's flag. The **laurel** is a favourite motif, along with stars, books and natural forms.

![The flag of Verna](data/images/verna-flag-f4affe1d.jpg "The flag of Verna: a gold compass rose inside a double ring, with four small ivory stars and a dotted circle, on a plain deep-green field. It suggests navigation, reason and scholarship rather than conquest, and the same compass-and-star device appears on banners, pins and official insignia.")

## What Vernans Wear

Vernan clothing is refined and practical: **long coats**, **fitted vests**, **neck scarves**, **spectacles**, **satchels**, **gloves**, **notebooks** and **instrument cases**. Quality materials, understated colours and things made to last are the rule.

Formal scholars wear **academic robes** with their faculty's colours and their college's insignia. Faculties and colleges use distinct colours, shown on robes, ribbons, scarves, pins and trim. Which colour belongs to which faculty is a matter of detail this entry does not settle.

![Vernan clothing: commoner, diplomat, academic and Expeditioner](data/images/verna-clothing-253dedfd.jpg "Four Vernans. A townsperson in comfortable, practical clothes of quality materials and understated colour, with a patterned scarf and satchel; a diplomat in elegant, restrained dress with the Republic's laurel insignia, carrying a document case; an academic in layered robes, sturdy and made to last; and a University Expeditioner equipped for distant lands and Gate phenomena. Note the spectacles, the faculty pins, the typical Vernan scarf patterning, the field medical bag and the notebooks and ink.")

The most important thing to notice is that **ordinary Vernans do not dress like professors**. Most of them are not professors. A Vernan printer, farmer or clerk dresses well and practically, and might wear a faculty pin only if a child is studying.

> **On the steps of a lecture hall**
>
> The two students had never met. Each glanced at the trim on the other's scarf.
>
> "Natural philosophy," said one.
>
> "Mathematics," said the other.
>
> There was a short, charged pause.
>
> "I suppose you think your models are evidence."
>
> "I suppose you think your observations are explanations."
>
> By the time the lecture began, they had missed the first twenty minutes, acquired an audience, and agreed to continue on Thursday.

## Precision Craft

Verna's economy suits precision rather than heavy industry: **instruments**, **optics**, **medicine**, **printing**, **fine engineering** and **publishing**. Vernan lenses, astronomical instruments, surgical tools and printed works are known well beyond its borders. The rest of its industrial life is still to be described.

> **In an instrument-maker's workshop**
>
> The young assistant held up the finished brass ring. "It's perfect."
>
> The instrument-maker took it, set it on the testing plate and watched the needle for a long time.
>
> "It is accurate to the limit of our measurement," she said. "That is not the same thing. When someone builds a better measuring plate, they will find out how imperfect it is." She handed it back. "Write down the limit. A buyer can trust an instrument that tells them how wrong it might be. They should never trust one that claims to be perfect."

## The Vernan Manner

The ideal Vernan public manner is **composed**, **evidence-minded**, **cautious**, **precise** and **sceptical**. Vernans are measured in speech, observant and politely doubtful. They say *"We do not know"* without embarrassment, and mean it as honesty rather than weakness. A very Vernan sentence, heard in laboratories and committee rooms alike, is:

> *"The evidence does not currently support that conclusion."*

## What Foreigners Get Wrong

The great foreign stereotype is that **every Vernan works at the University**. Vernans find this endlessly irritating. The Republic has farms, workshops, printing houses, hospitals, courts and town councils, and a great many Vernans would be hard pressed to name more than two faculties. The University may be Verna's most famous export, but Verna is a country, not a campus, and it would like to be visited as one.
